title: Greet with a default argument
description: Write a function `greet(name="Guest")` that returns `f"Hello, {name}!"`, defaulting to 'Guest' when called with no argument.
hints: Idea to consider: a default parameter value, set once in the function signature
def greet(name='Guest') already gives name the value 'Guest' whenever the caller doesn't supply one - no need for an if/else inside the function body to check whether an argument was passed.
Return f'Hello, {name}!' - the default in the signature handles the no-argument case automatically.
expected_behavior: Returns a greeting using name, or 'Guest' if no name is given.
explanation: A default parameter value is evaluated once and used automatically whenever the caller omits that argument - it replaces an if/else that would otherwise check 'was name provided?' inside the function.
